A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPG research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite reformatting and section relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original RL fine-tuning results on four reasoning benchmarks, component ablations, training dynamics, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds coding evaluations, comparator experiments, sensitivity studies, computational measurements, and validation-based checkpoint evaluation.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the SPG objectives remain unchanged: ELBO for positive advantages, EUBO or its ELBO mixture for negative advantages, and block-wise masking. Coding experiments apply the existing method; the additional training variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: v1 covers mathematical and logical reasoning through GSM8K, MATH500, Countdown, and Sudoku. v3 adds coding training on KodCode-Light-RL-10K and evaluation on HumanEval and MBPP, substantially extending coverage to executable program generation.

E2.justification: v3 adds StepWise, a reimplementation of LLaDOU's trajectory-level RL component, reward-shifted REINFORCE and GRPO, and UniGRPO with block-wise masking (Tables 6, 7, and 22). These expand the evaluated alternatives beyond v1's retained comparators. The complete LLaDOU system, including learned decoding order, is not evaluated.

E3.justification: The original main evaluation protocol remains. v3 adds an evaluation splitting each original reasoning test set equally into validation and test subsets, selecting checkpoints on validation accuracy (Table 23). New experiments also introduce full fine-tuning with smaller learning rates, removal of prompt masking, and four rather than two Monte Carlo samples.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained bound, masking, hyperparameter, inference, and diversity analyses, v3 tests dependence on LoRA, prompt masking, and Monte Carlo sample count. Reward shifting and block-wise UniGRPO probe alternative explanations for SPG's advantages; checkpoint-selection and computational-cost analyses further strengthen the supplementary evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report rolling-window means and standard deviations over 50 training steps in Figures 3, 7, and 9. Neither introduces independent-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new Monte Carlo sample-count ablation concerns training estimation, not repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: The original results are retained, but substantial new results appear. At length 256, Table 2 reports HumanEval accuracy of 41.5 for SPG/EUBO versus 39.6 for UniGRPO, and MBPP accuracy of 50.6 for SPG/Mixture versus 45.9 for WD1. Further tables add comparator, ablation, timing, and validation-selected results; the latter use different splits and are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: The EUBO theorem, mixture-variance proposition, proofs, and toy-example derivations are retained. Appendix F adds theoretical assertions about reward-shift invariance under termination and terminal-reward assumptions, and about RLOO unbiasedness, without supplying new proofs.

C1.justification: The introduction extends the empirical contribution from four reasoning benchmarks to include two coding benchmarks, claiming gains of 1.9 percentage points on HumanEval and 4.7 on MBPP. The central SPG and block-wise masking claims, abstract, and conclusion otherwise retain their earlier substance.

C2.justification: Appendix F adds substantive discussion of unresolved KL/trust-region stabilization, remaining group-relative advantage bias, and proposed exploration disadvantages of reward shifting. Appendices H.2–H.3 add interpretations of prompt masking, sampling cost and stability, and possible test-set overfitting from checkpoint selection. These go substantially beyond v1's bound-mixture explanations.

D1.justification: v3 adds the coding dataset link, formatting and unit-test reward rules, blocked-module handling, and a 6,000-update coding budget. It also specifies full-fine-tuning learning rates, measured runtimes with hardware context, and a project-page link. The existing code link and core implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix C and Table 5 substantially expand comparison of RL objectives, likelihood estimators, and masking strategies. v3 positions LLaDOU's learned decoding order as complementary to SPG while contrasting its costly trajectory-level updates. It also adds literature supporting the RLOO discussion, coding evaluation, and LoRA analysis; the original related-work section is largely retained.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. Related work moves from the main text to Appendix A, while new overview, discussion, and evaluation sections organize the additions. Local explanatory expansions, acknowledgements, and front-matter edits do not amount to extensive rewriting of the original narrative.

P2.justification: v3 adopts an ICLR layout with different title treatment, typography, margins, running headers, and figure/table placement. It adds tables for coding, algorithm comparison, new baselines, and supplementary tests. The original nine figures are retained and resized or relocated; retained inference-table groups are reordered.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens empirical credibility and scope. The validation-selected evaluation addresses sensitivity to v1's test-based checkpoint selection, while StepWise, reward-shifting, and block-wise UniGRPO comparisons better test competing explanations for SPG's advantages. Coding results and implementation-sensitivity studies provide evidence beyond the original reasoning setup, and measured runtimes substantiate efficiency discussion. These are consequential improvements in validation, although the main results still use the original selection protocol and independent-run uncertainty remains unreported.
